ev.q: The number of excess stroke deaths was largest for non-Hispanic blacks and As/PIs aged 35-84 years
Expected deaths were calculated by multiplying the number of persons in each age-specific racial/ethnic group by the death rates in the corresponding non-Hispanic white group.
Relative risks were calculated by dividing the death rate for each age-specific group by the corresponding death rate for non-Hispanic whites.
Non-Hispanic whites in each age group were the referent group.
AIs/ANs had almost twice the relative risk for stroke mortality than non-Hispanic whites among persons aged 35-44 years
Non-Hispanic blacks had approximately four times the relative risk for persons aged 35-54 years
Age-specific excess deaths were calculated by subtracting the observed deaths from the expected deaths
The 1997 death certificate data were used to determine excess death and relative risk for stroke mortality by racial/ethnic group

methods_quotes.q: Expected deaths were calculated by multiplying the number of persons in each age-specific racial/ethnic group by the death rates in the corresponding non-Hispanic white group.
Relative risks were calculated by dividing the death rate for each age-specific group by the corresponding death rate for non-Hispanic whites.
Age-specific excess deaths were calculated by subtracting the observed deaths from the expected deaths for each age-specific group.
Relative risk is the ratio of the stroke death rate of the minority group compared with that of the non-Hispanic white population
